area.title: East porch
area.subtitle: A lamp is meant to be seen
area.blurb: Juniper’s lamp. You arrive here so today’s line can be seen.
area.intro: The east porch is where a line can be seen. Juniper keeps the lamp.

lesson.title: The porch lamp
lesson.idea: a city on a hill is meant to be seen
lesson.claim: A lamp is meant to be seen.
lesson.plain: A lamp is meant to be seen.

easy.learn: Jesus uses an ordinary lamp and a city on a hill. Public without being proud.

match.sentence: A lamp is meant to be seen.

hold.why: A lamp and a hill city are meant to be seen.
hold.claimMiss: We are told to become the sun.
Light is only for insiders behind a door.
hold.whyMiss: The picture is a command to boast.
A hidden lamp is the point of the saying.

lesson.title: Porch gems
lesson.idea: Jesus taught with pictures you can hold
lesson.claim: Jesus taught with pictures you can hold.
lesson.plain: Jesus taught with pictures you can hold.

easy.learn: A lamp is seen. Seed meets different hearts. The cup is poured for many — gift, not wage.

match.sentence: Jesus taught with pictures you can hold.

hold.why: Lamp, seed, and cup are gifts you can hold.
hold.claimMiss: Pictures are only decoration.
Mercy is a wage you finish earning.
hold.whyMiss: Every heart is the same soil.
A hidden lamp is the point.

lesson.title: A handful of seed
lesson.idea: the same word meets very different hearts
lesson.claim: The same word meets different soils; some seed is lost.
lesson.plain: The same word meets different soils. Some seed is lost.

easy.learn: This Jesus story invites hearing. It does not flatter every field.

match.sentence: The same word meets different soils; some seed is lost.

hold.why: Not every field is good soil.
hold.claimMiss: Every field is guaranteed a harvest.
Lost seed means the sower failed.
hold.whyMiss: Good soil is a slogan, not a way of hearing.
Jesus never names withering or birds.

lesson.title: Who is near
lesson.idea: neighbor is the one who shows mercy
lesson.claim: Mercy makes a neighbor; pedigree does not.
lesson.plain: Mercy makes a neighbor. Pedigree does not.

easy.learn: Jesus asks who *proved* to be a neighbor — the one who showed mercy.

match.sentence: Mercy makes a neighbor; pedigree does not.

hold.why: Jesus asks who showed mercy — that one is neighbor.
hold.claimMiss: The priest who passed by is the measure.
Neighbor is settled before anyone crosses the road.
hold.whyMiss: Mercy is unrelated to the question.
The wounded man must first classify the helper.
